newsitem.title: JAPAN: SPEED SKATING-SCHENK WINS FOURTH STRAIGHT VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-SCHENK WINS FOURTH STRAIGHT VICTORY.

text.p: Franziska Schenk of Germany took her fourth straight World Cup victory in a speed skating competition on Sunday.
In the women's 1,000 metres, Schenk lost her balance briefly as she came out of the turn after 300 metres but she still triumphed for the second day at Ikaho with a time of one minute 21.73 seconds.
Kyoko Shimazaki of Japan became the first skater to finish within a second of Schenk this season, crossing the line 0.57 seconds behind while Tomomi Okazaki was a further 0.05 seconds back for third.
Manabu Horii completed a Japanese sweep of the first four men's 500-metre races of the season and compatriot Okazaki notched up Japan's third straight victory in the women's event.
Horii clocked a rink record of 36.43 seconds at the outdoor arena to win by a comfortable, 0.26-second margin over Russian world sprint champion Sergey Klevchenya.
His Japanese team mate and world record holder Hiroyasu Shimizu, a winner on Saturday, pulled out of Sunday's races with an injury to a muscle in his left knee.
Jaegal Sung-yeol took third place in 36.73, then went on to grab a second straight victory for South Korea in the men's 1,000 with a time of 1:15.01 in near windless conditions.
Okazaki, who was fifth on Saturday, won the women's 500 with a rink record of 39.75 seconds.
Norway's top sprint skater Grunde Njos withdrew from the event on Sunday after suffering head injuries from a crash during a race on Saturday, team officials said.
Njos, 29, lost consciousness for several minutes after crashing into a barricade when he failed to negotiate the final turn.
